thought.text: The timed-out foreground build appears to have taken down the whole process group, including my backgrounded backend build. Let me verify:

reasoning_content:
Whoa, several things happened:
1. `docker images` shows nothing (no temurin or corretto images)
2. The docker build process is gone!

Did the cache mount test's build kill the main backend build? No wait — Docker builds run in separate daemons, so they shouldn't interfere with each other. But the main build was pulling the base image. Could it be that the cache test's build consumed the daemon's concurrent pull bandwidth, and the main build died?

No, that's not it. Let me check the backend build log and see what happened. Also, the fact that `docker images` doesn't list any images means that at the point I ran it, the main build hadn't yet pulled the base image to completion? But the log said the temurin layer was 89MB/91MB...

Hmm, actually maybe the timeout killed the shell, but `docker build` was launched in the foreground (not nohup!) — in my cache test command, the first `docker build` was in the foreground, and when the 600-second timeout killed the shell, its child process (docker build) might have been killed as well. And the main backend build (pid 3328) was nohup'd, so it should survive... but it's not in the process list.

Wait, let me re-read: the main build was launched with `nohup docker build ... &`. The timeout killed the shell of the cache test command. Hmm, but why isn't pid 3328 there?

Ah, wait. I think I got it: when the terminal command timed out, it might have killed the entire process group, which could have included the backgrounded nohup process too (nohup only protects from SIGHUP, not SIGKILL to the process group). It's possible the 600-second timeout's kill signal (SIGKILL to the process group) killed both the cache test build and the main backend build.

Let me check the end of the build log and the state of docker.

action.command: tail -5 /tmp/backend-build.log; echo "==="; docker ps -a | head; echo "=== docker system df ==="; docker system df 2>/dev/null; echo "=== all node/pnpm procs ==="; ps aux | grep -E "pnpm|node /usr" | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2,$11,$12}'
